subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should isolated cron setup use a bounded share of the job timeout budget, remain fixed at 60 seconds, or become operator-configurable?
rationale: Changing this default affects both reliability for slow cold starts and the amount of cron capacity a truly stuck setup can occupy, so code inspection alone cannot choose the permanent product policy.

options.title: Accept bounded setup budget
options.body: Land PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 or equivalent so long isolated setup can progress beyond 60s while staying capped.

options.title: Keep 60s fixed default
options.body: Reject the longer wait and instead focus on surfacing exact setup phases or requiring users to reduce cron/provider cold-start pressure.

options.title: Make it configurable
options.body: Add an operator-tunable watchdog with schema/docs/migration proof, accepting the extra config surface despite the repo's high config bar.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded setup budget
recommendation.body: Land PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219 or equivalent so long isolated setup can progress beyond 60s while staying capped.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a cron runtime policy/default tradeoff, and steipete has the strongest sampled history across the cron timer/watchdog surface.
